_why: The one proposal from the gloss sweep that Opus 4.8 never returned a verdict for: shard 007 emitted 24 verdicts where 25 were required. Verified against external sources instead of a second model, at Josh's request, because the proposed gloss was model-authored -- kaikki lists only 'to weave' for this verb, so there was no dictionary sense available to re-pick.
_definitions: PONS de-en: primary translation 'to interweave sth'
Langenscheidt de-en: 'to weave sth into sth, to interweave (or interlace) sth with sth'
DWDS: five senses, all joining-by-weaving; word marked selten
Duden: weak inflection for the handcraft sense, strong for the figurative
_attested_uses: DWDS corpus: all five citations figurative, none literal textile weaving -- 'das sehr eng miteinander verwobene Establishment' (Die Zeit, 2005); 'unser Schicksal so verwoben wie mit dem tschechischen Volk' (1996); 'Seine private Geschichte ist verwoben mit dem Untergang des alten Oesterreich' (Die Zeit, 1970); 'Das Spiel sei eng mit dem Film verwoben' (SZ, 2003); 'sie verwebten sich in meine Traeume' (Bischoff, 1912)
Reverso Context, infinitive verweben, frequency-ranked renderings: interweave > weave > intertwine > weave together > entwine > interlace > inweave > twine
Reverso Context, participle verwoben: interwoven > woven > entwined > interweaved > interrelated > weaved > interweaving > intermeshed > intertwining

Reverso attested pairs: 'Streicher und Gitarren verweben sich wie vom Baum herabfallende Blaetter' -> 'Strings and guitars interweave like leaves falling down from a tree'; 'Filmtypische Elemente verweben sich mit Zeitgenoessischem Tanz' -> 'Typical film elements interweave with contemporary dance'; 'Roest- und Kaffeearomen, verwoben mit Eiche' -> 'Roasted and coffee flavours interwoven with oak'
Linguee published bilingual pairs: interwoven dominant, then interrelated, intermeshed, woven together
Literal textile use survives mainly as the nominalized Verweben in craft prose ('das Verweben verschiedener Garne'), not as the finite verb in general text
_decision: Three states, each evidence-driven. Proposed 'interweave' (model-authored; kaikki lists only 'to weave', so no sense was available to re-pick). Briefly widened to 'interweave, interlace' on Langenscheidt's dictionary listing, then narrowed again when attested uses showed interlace ranks sixth on Reverso and appears in no Linguee pair -- dictionary-attested is not the same as used. Final gloss pairs the dominant rendering with intertwine, which ranks third and carries the figurative sense the corpus shows dominates.
_note: weben itself ships 'weave', so the pre-correction gloss made the base verb and its ver- derivative identical.

verweben.why: ver- carries joining-by-weaving; kaikki's bare 'to weave' is weben and collided with it -- both verbs shipped the identical gloss. Every DWDS corpus citation is figurative, and interweave/interwoven is the dominant published rendering.

_verified_via: WebSearch, WebFetch (DWDS, PONS, Linguee), and Chrome MCP for Reverso Context, which 403s WebFetch
_register_of_use: The finite verb is effectively FIGURATIVE-ONLY in attested general text. Every DWDS corpus citation (5/5) and every free Reverso example for the infinitive (6/6) is figurative -- love and friendship, film elements, narrative strands, fates, institutions. The literal textile sense is attested in DICTIONARIES (DWDS senses 1-3, with constructed examples like 'Goldfaeden in eine Decke verweben') but survives in real prose mainly as the nominalized 'das Verweben von Faeden' in craft writing. Reverso's remaining examples sit behind a registration wall that was not created. The gloss is NOT marked figurative, deliberately: 'interweave' and 'intertwine' both read naturally in either register, so nothing misleads, and appending a usage label such as '(figurative)' would reproduce the leaked-dictionary-apparatus defect this whole sweep was removing -- the brief rates entmieten 'of a landlord' as high severity for exactly that.
